judgements.justification: In B, Reviewer_6CYj faulted the paper for giving 'no clear cue' how the discriminator contributes, but Table 3 isolates it (22.60 to 23.53 BLEU-4); no A reviewer made this error.
A's AC gave a spotlight over ratings 7, 6, 7, 7 with no rating above 7, no reviewer arguing for an award, and no argument for the tier beyond 'a novel algorithm design I have never seen'.
A's Reviewer_pdQY praised the 'comprehensive evaluation' and the 'new' problem at face value, and A's meta-review paraphrased pdQY's and Reviewer_6a7g's praise ('seems very novel').
Both committees received the same rebuttal material, including the zero-shot table; no flaw was disclosed to one committee only.
A's Reviewer_pdQY asked for the visual-hint F1 results, the direct test of the central claim; the authors replied that no ground truth exists, and no one in A pressed or weighed it.
No score moved after the rebuttal in either committee.
Only B raised that DH-VQG is missing from the human study and Section 3.4, that DH-GAN ties its own Generator in Table 2, and that augmentation gains are 0.1 to 0.2 points; no one in A raised these.

Both committees saw the same zero-shot table on the usefulness of generated questions; A's AC called the rebuttal 'a particularly good job', while B's AC said the results 'again miss comparison to prior work'.
B's AC followed a unanimous reject consensus, and A's AC added an own assessment; neither resolved a split by adopting one reviewer.
No reviewer changed a score after reading the other reviews.
The authors answered every reviewer and followed up with Reviewer_W4CH; the reviewer, not the authors, failed to reply.
Reviews in both committees gave specifics; A's Reviewer_Kags was thin but acknowledged the response, and B's unedited reviews rested on checkable points.
B's AC rejected over unanimous below-threshold ratings 5, 4, 5, 5.
Neither AC decided by a borderline mean against a stated contrary view.
B's low scores rested on novelty over DH-VQG and the weak evaluation, which are central, not peripheral.
Both committees read the paper as a VQG methods contribution; they differed on what it had to show, not on its kind.
No A reviewer raised a score on the rebuttal, and A's confidences were 4 to 5.
B's reviewers and AC required the paper to show that VQG helps downstream VQA, judging the task's value, while A asked this only once and did not require it.
A's Reviewer_pdQY called double-hint VQG 'new', but the paper credits that setting to Kai et al. [20]; A's AC repeated the error in the meta-review.
No reviewer acknowledged that the rebuttal resolved their main concern.
The authors promised to add the DH-VQG comparison in revision; B's AC rejected because the comparison was missing, while A did not require it.
Reviewer_W4CH offered to reconsider but stated no changed position; no reviewer's stated stance diverged from the score.
Neither AC used an off-record extra reviewer.

reasoning: The split comes from A's uncritical reading and A's AC raising the tier: A's reviewers accepted the paper's framing, including a wrong novelty claim (R19, R03), let a non-answer on the central claim pass (R05), and A's AC gave an unargued spotlight over ratings capped at 7 (R02). B checked the evaluation against DH-VQG and raised issues A never saw (R07), weighed the same zero-shot evidence and the promised DH-VQG comparison oppositely (R08, R21), and demanded downstream value for VQG (R18). One minor wrong claim in B (R01) did not drive the outcome. The stage 1 candidates (effect sizes, missing baseline, task significance, AC upgrade, rebuttal read oppositely) all map to existing reasons, so no reason is added.
